chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so fresh dates were brought to him. He began eating from them and drinking water, and he handed me the bowl. I disliked returning it, so I drank until he did that repeatedly.

He said, so I said: 'I used to have excess phlegm, so I complained about it to Ahran, the physician of Al-Hajjaj.' He said to me: 'Do you have a palm tree in your orchard?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Are there palm trees in it?' I said: 'Yes.' So he said to me: 'Count for me what is in it.'

So I counted until I reached Al-Hayrun (a type of date). He said to me: 'Eat seven of them whenever you intend to sleep, and do not drink water.' So I did that, and I wanted to spit but I was unable to do so. So I complained to him about that, so he said to me: 'Drink a little water and hold back until your constitution becomes balanced.'
So I did that. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for me, had it not been for the water, I would not care if I did not taste it.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, title of Imam al-Sadiq

ai.seo_question: What is the medical and spiritual benefit of eating dates with water according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia tradition of *Tibb al-Nabawi* (Prophetic Medicine), where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the physiological benefits of consuming fresh dates (*rutab*) with water to balance the body's humors. The narrative highlights a practical medical anecdote regarding the treatment of excess phlegm, demonstrating how dietary adjustments can restore constitutional equilibrium, while the Imam’s personal preference underscores the spiritual and physical purity associated with this Sunnah. It serves as a key reference for understanding the interplay between physical health and spiritual discipline in Shia jurisprudence and medicine.
